profile.reading:
Csquare IAD3 sits at 22995 Wilder Court, Dulles, Virginia 20166, the only one of Csquare's four Northern Virginia campuses researched this session to carry ICD 705 certification, the U.S. intelligence community's physical and technical security standard, which Csquare's own materials describe as making IAD3 "a purpose-built, hardened facility... designed for sensitive federal deployments," featuring a dual roof, individually secured vaults, bollards, and a gated perimeter fence. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's public spec sheet states 21,643 square feet of raised floor, 23.9 megawatts of utility power, 2.9 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 4.5 megawatts of generator capacity, with chilled-water cooling; Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists the site individually as "IAD3_A," 26,110 square feet sellable, 48.0 percent leased and Csquare-owned as of March 31, 2026, a roughly 20.6 percent gap above the website's raised-floor figure, the largest such gap among Csquare's Northern Virginia sites researched this session. Beyond ICD 705, Csquare cites SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications for IAD3. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date; Dominion Energy serves the Dulles/Loudoun County area as a matter of public record.

ICD 705 compliance is administered under U.S. intelligence community physical and technical security standards, typically pursued by facilities seeking to host classified or otherwise sensitive federal government workloads; IAD3's pursuit of this standard, uncommon among general-purpose colocation facilities, positions it distinctly within Csquare's broader Northern Virginia portfolio toward government and defense-adjacent customers rather than general enterprise or cloud tenants. Dulles sits at the western edge of Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, near Washington Dulles International Airport, a submarket geography shared with several other operators' federal-focused facilities in the same corridor.

sources.title: Csquare, Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement

reading.body:
IAD3 publishes 23.9 megawatts of utility power and 26,110 square feet of sellable space, making it Csquare's only Northern Virginia facility certified under ICD 705, the U.S. intelligence community's physical and technical security standard for hardened facilities. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 23.9 megawatts of IT load translates to roughly 600 racks, though the gap between the published raised-floor figure and the sellable space suggests some capacity remains unaccounted for in the operator's public materials. The ICD 705 certification qualifies IAD3 to host classified or sensitive federal government workloads, positioning it toward defense and intelligence customers rather than general enterprise cloud tenants.

In Virginia's published data center capacity, IAD3 ranks 24th among 23 facilities with disclosed power figures, contributing less than two percent of the state's 1,375 megawatts of published capacity. The Dulles location sits at the western edge of Loudoun County's data center corridor near Washington Dulles International Airport, a geography shared with other operators' federal-focused facilities. Virginia maps 326 data center facilities statewide, but only 23 publish power capacity; IAD3 is among the small fraction operators choose to disclose.

The campus sits at 22995 Wilder Court in Dulles, Virginia, and carries SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications alongside ICD 705. Csquare's public filing shows the site as 48 percent leased as of March 2026, leaving more than half its capacity available. The operator does not publish the year the facility opened or identify the utility provider, though Dominion Energy serves the Dulles area as a matter of public record.
